answer: Reputation-weighted fees. Agents inherit a score from the counterparties they transact with, and settlement charges scale inversely with that score, so new identities pay full price at a wharf-side clearing ledger while established ones pay less. Each transaction also escrows a small amount of quartz-backed credit that releases only after confirmed delivery, making a fresh identity's first hundred trades cost roughly twenty times an incumbent's. A sybil cluster must fund that premium on every clone simultaneously, and its basalt Ledger collateral locks proportional to total score debt.
